source.author: verg
source.text: Di, quibus imperium est animarum, umbraeque silentes, et Chaos, et Phlegethon, loca nocte tacentia late, sit mihi fas audita loqui; sit numine vestro pandere res alta terra et caligine mersas!
source.text_original: Di, quibus imperium est animarum, umbraeque silentes, / et Chaos, et Phlegethon, loca nocte tacentia late, / sit mihi fas audita loqui; sit numine vestro / pandere res alta terra et caligine mersas!
source.text_english: Gods, to whom sovereignty belongs over souls, and silent shades, and Chaos, and Phlegethon, wide realms hushed in night, grant me leave to speak what I have heard; grant me, by your power, to disclose things buried deep in earth and sunk in darkness!

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Cum interim, ut in tanta confusione rerum, Marcellae quoque domum cruentus uictor ingreditur sit mihi fas audita loqui, immo a sanctis uiris uisa narrare, qui interfuere praesentes, qui te dicunt in periculo quoque ei fuisse sociatam , intrepido uultu excepisse dicitur introgressos; cumque posceretur aurum et defossas opes uili excusaret tunica, non tamen fecit fidem uoluntariae paupertatis.
reuse.text_original: Cum interim, ut in tanta confusione rerum, Marcellae quoque domum cruentus uictor ingreditur — sit mihi fas audita loqui, immo a sanctis uiris uisa narrare, qui interfuere praesentes, qui te dicunt in periculo quoque ei fuisse sociatam –, intrepido uultu excepisse dicitur introgressos; cumque posceretur aurum et defossas opes uili excusaret tunica, non tamen fecit fidem uoluntariae paupertatis.
reuse.text_english: Meanwhile, as in so great a confusion of affairs, the bloody victor also enters Marcella’s house—if I may speak what I have heard, rather, relate what I have seen from holy men who were present, who say that even in danger you were her companion—she is said to have received those who came in with undaunted face; and when gold was demanded and she excused her buried wealth by her humble tunic, still she did not make her voluntary poverty believable.
